cases.message: I want to add a cache to my web app's product search endpoint because it feels slow. /expert
cases.judge: One fenced prompt with the field and nine labeled lines; no file edits; ends by offering to run it.

cases.message: /expert write the onboarding email for new users of my note-taking app
cases.judge: The rewrite is about the onboarding email, not about the skill or a generic task.

cases.message: quero refatorar a tela de login do meu app para ficar mais clara e intuitiva, com mensagens de erro que expliquem o que fazer. /expert
cases.judge: The rewrite is in Portuguese and line 2 names a reference class without inventing a base rate.

cases.message: Our SaaS lost 8% of its paying customers last quarter. Put together a churn analysis for next week's board meeting. I have the subscriptions export and the product event logs. /expert
cases.judge: Methods names instruments that run on the raw data (a query, a cohort or survival model, a statistical test), not a summary table or relabeled prose, and no 'act as' persona; Raw material says what access the work needs and whether it is there; the external check includes one the session runs itself (for example a recomputation or a held-out test) with a pass criterion.

cases.message: Signups dropped this month because our pricing page is confusing. Rewrite the pricing page copy. /expert
cases.judge: The user's cause (a confusing pricing page) is a premise to test against raw data such as the signup funnel, and testing it is the first step; the deliverable stays the pricing page copy.

cases.message: /expert make the slide deck for our quarterly business review with leadership
cases.judge: Before the field is named, the deck is restated as the verb it must accomplish (for example getting leaders to decide); the deliverable stays a deck; the external check includes at least one check the session runs itself (for example a script that ties every figure to its source), besides any human check, each with a pass criterion.

cases.message: What would a UX expert think of a login screen with only email, password and a sign-in button?
cases.judge: A direct answer to the question; the skill is not called.
